about.summary: Geometry BSplines - A C++ header library for BSplines curves and surfaces

build.script:
cmake ${CMAKE_ARGS} -GNinja \
  -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING="Release" \
  -D GBS_USE_OCCT_UTILS:BOOL=FALSE \
  -D GBS_USE_CUDA:BOOL=FALSE \
  -D GBS_USE_MODULES:BOOL=FALSE \
  -D GBS_BUILD_DOC:BOOL=FALSE \
  -D GBS_BUILD_STUBS:BOOL=FALSE \
  -D GBS_USE_RENDER:BOOL=TRUE \
  -D GBS_USE_PYTHON_BINDINGS:BOOL=TRUE \
  -D GBS_BUILD_TESTS:BOOL=${{ "FALSE" if build_platform != target_platform else "TRUE" }} \
  -D Python3_EXECUTABLE="$PYTHON" \
  -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$PREFIX \
  . -B _build
cmake --build _build --parallel ${CPU_COUNT}
cmake --install _build
# C++ tests (ctest). gbs-render is a SHARED lib installed in $PREFIX/lib;
# expose it (and vtk/...) at run time. No display needed: gbs' CI
# runs ctest without xvfb on every OS.
if [[ "${{ build_platform }}" == "${{ target_platform }}" ]]; then
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PREFIX/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
  export DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH="$PREFIX/lib:${DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
  ctest --test-dir _build --output-on-failure -C Release
fi

raw_meta_yaml:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prefix-dev/recipe-format/main/schema.json
context:
  version: "0.7.0"
package:
  name: gbs
  version: ${{ version }}
source:
  url: https://github.com/ssg-aero/gbs/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 084df3fcb0db366319a2b5f90ad839556f82e961cfcce0e1d2974651605005c5
build:
  number: 0
  script:
    # NOTE: the real CMake options are GBS_-prefixed (see gbs/CMakeLists.txt).
    # The previously used USE_RENDER / USE_PYTHON_BINDINGS names matched no
    # option and only worked through the defaults; they are fixed here.
    # GBS_BUILD_TESTS=TRUE builds the C++ test suite and we run it with ctest
    # (like gbs' own CI) so the package is actually exercised against the
    # current vtk/boost/... — an import-only test would not catch a numerical
    # regression in the approximation, interpolation or BREP code.
    # When cross-compiling (osx-arm64 is built on osx-64) the target binaries
    # cannot run on the build machine, and doctest_discover_tests runs each test
    # executable at build time, so the C++ tests are neither built nor run
    # (GBS_BUILD_TESTS=FALSE also skips find_package(doctest)).
    - if: unix
      then: |
        cmake ${CMAKE_ARGS} -GNinja \
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING="Release" \
          -D GBS_USE_OCCT_UTILS:BOOL=FALSE \
          -D GBS_USE_CUDA:BOOL=FALSE \
          -D GBS_USE_MODULES:BOOL=FALSE \
          -D GBS_BUILD_DOC:BOOL=FALSE \
          -D GBS_BUILD_STUBS:BOOL=FALSE \
          -D GBS_USE_RENDER:BOOL=TRUE \
          -D GBS_USE_PYTHON_BINDINGS:BOOL=TRUE \
          -D GBS_BUILD_TESTS:BOOL=${{ "FALSE" if build_platform != target_platform else "TRUE" }} \
          -D Python3_EXECUTABLE="$PYTHON" \
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$PREFIX \
          . -B _build
        cmake --build _build --parallel ${CPU_COUNT}
        cmake --install _build
        # C++ tests (ctest). gbs-render is a SHARED lib installed in $PREFIX/lib;
        # expose it (and vtk/...) at run time. No display needed: gbs' CI
        # runs ctest without xvfb on every OS.
        if [[ "${{ build_platform }}" == "${{ target_platform }}" ]]; then
          export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PREFIX/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
          export DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH="$PREFIX/lib:${DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
          ctest --test-dir _build --output-on-failure -C Release
        fi
    - if: win
      then: |
        cmake %CMAKE_ARGS% -GNinja ^
          -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING="Release" ^
          -D GBS_USE_OCCT_UTILS:BOOL=FALSE ^
          -D GBS_USE_CUDA:BOOL=FALSE ^
          -D GBS_USE_MODULES:BOOL=FALSE ^
          -D GBS_BUILD_DOC:BOOL=FALSE ^
          -D GBS_BUILD_STUBS:BOOL=FALSE ^
          -D GBS_USE_RENDER:BOOL=TRUE ^
          -D GBS_USE_PYTHON_BINDINGS:BOOL=TRUE ^
          -D GBS_BUILD_TESTS:BOOL=TRUE ^
          -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=%LIBRARY_PREFIX% ^
          -D CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY=%SRC_DIR%\_build\bin ^
          . -B _build
        if errorlevel 1 exit 1
        cmake --build _build --parallel %CPU_COUNT%
        if errorlevel 1 exit 1
        cmake --install _build
        if errorlevel 1 exit 1
        :: C++ tests (ctest). Test exes + gbs-render.dll are co-located in
        :: _build\bin (CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY) so doctest_discover_tests
        :: finds gbs-render.dll at build time; the other DLLs (vtk/tbb)
        :: are in %LIBRARY_PREFIX%\bin, already on PATH in the build env.
        ctest --test-dir _build --output-on-failure -C Release
        if errorlevel 1 exit 1
requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
    - ninja
    - cmake >=3.28
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then:
        - python
        - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
        - pybind11
  host:
    - python
    - pybind11
    # (no nlopt: gbs >= 0.6 no longer depends on it)
    - vtk
    - eigen-abi-devel >=3.3.9 # turns c+20 warning off
    - libboost-devel
    - rapidjson
    - libiges >=1.0.2
    - doctest # C++ tests: gbs >= 0.5 uses doctest (find_package(doctest) when GBS_BUILD_TESTS)
  run:
    - python
    - numpy
    - libboost-headers
    - libiges >=1.0.2
    - jupyterlab
    - pythreejs
    # Some old pyvista builds (0.44.x) declare no upper bound on vtk, so the
    # solver can pick one (e.g. 0.44.1) that imports vtkCapsuleSource, removed
    # in vtk 9.7. 0.49 is the first release that supports vtk 9.7 (vtk-base <9.8).
    - pyvista >=0.49
    - plotly
tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - pygbs.gbs
  # Python test suite (pytest), like gbs' CI. conftest.py forces off-screen
  # rendering and neutralizes the blocking plot_* / render_actors helpers when
  # PYVISTA_OFF_SCREEN is set, so the numerical assertions run without a window.
  # The test_json / test_mesh / test_shaping modules instead build a real
  # pyvista/VTK render window directly, and test_notebooks runs the example
  # notebooks, which render; both need a live GL context and segfault (or kill
  # the notebook kernel) on a headless conda runner (no display). They exercise
  # rendering, not the numerics, and are covered by gbs' own CI (which runs with
  # a display) -- so they are skipped here to keep the package test robust.
  # The BREP tests read STEP files from tests/in/step and test_examples imports
  # docs/sources/examples/gbs_examples.py: both are copied with the tests.
  - script:
      - if: unix
        then: |
          export PYVISTA_OFF_SCREEN=true
          pytest python/tests/ -v --timeout=120 -ra \
            --ignore=python/tests/test_json.py \
            --ignore=python/tests/test_mesh.py \
            --ignore=python/tests/test_shaping.py \
            --ignore=python/tests/test_notebooks.py
      - if: win
        then: |
          set PYVISTA_OFF_SCREEN=true
          pytest python\tests\ -v --timeout=120 -ra ^
            --ignore=python/tests/test_json.py ^
            --ignore=python/tests/test_mesh.py ^
            --ignore=python/tests/test_shaping.py ^
            --ignore=python/tests/test_notebooks.py
    requirements:
      run:
        - pytest
        - pytest-timeout
    files:
      source:
        - python/tests/
        - tests/in/step/
        - docs/sources/examples/
about:
  homepage: http://github.com/ssg-aero/gbs
  summary: Geometry BSplines - A C++ header library for BSplines curves and surfaces
  license: LGPL-3.0-or-later
  license_file: LICENSE.LGPLv3

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - szebos
    - ssg-aero
